reason: The text explicitly demonstrates that non-leaders exercise significant agency. The common people (עם) and their wives cry out and express their grievances actively; various groups among the people voice their own decisions and intentions ('let us take grain and eat'); the people themselves enslave their own children (כבשים את בניהם) as an independent action; and crucially, the assembly (קהל) affirms Nehemiah's reform ('they said Amen and praised the Lord') and carries out the agreement ('the people did according to this word'). While Nehemiah as governor takes leadership action, the text clearly portrays ordinary people exercising their own agency in both problematic actions (economic oppression) and in responding to and implementing reforms.
